# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)

  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).

20:pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.
21:- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
22:  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
23:  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
24:  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
25:- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
26:  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
27:- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
28:- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
29:- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
30:- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.
31:### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`
32:The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.
33:`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`
34:```yaml
35:# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
36:# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
37:validate:
38:  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
39:  next: load
40:load:
41:  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
42:  next: apply
43:apply:
44:  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
45:  govern: [ transaction ]
46:  next: save
47:save:
48:  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
49:  govern: [ transaction ]
50:  next: respond
51:respond:
52:  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
53:```
54:```java
55:// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
56:public class ValidateOwner {
57:  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
58:    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
59:  }
60:}
61:public class LoadOwner {
62:  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
63:      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
64:    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
65:    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
66:    ownerOut.set(owner);
67:  }
68:}
69:public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
70:  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
71:    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
72:    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
73:  }
74:}
75:public class SaveOwner {
76:  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
77:    repository.save(owner);
78:  }
79:}
80:public class RespondWithOwner {
81:  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
82:    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
83:  }
84:}
85:```
86:`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`
87:```yaml
88:handle:
89:  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
90:```
91:```java
92:public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
93:  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
94:      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
95:    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
96:  }
97:}
98:```
99:### Step wiring
100:Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
101:point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
102:method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
103:`method:`.
104:- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
105:  as `@Parameter T`.
106:- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
107:  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
108:  branch; not calling it short-circuits.
109:### Function parameters
110:Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:
111:- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
112:- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
113:- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
114:  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
115:  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
116:- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
117:  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.
118:### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`
119:Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
120:into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):
121:- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
122:- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
123:  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
124:- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
125:  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.
126:### Naming
127:Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
128:absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
129:publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
130:`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).
131:Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
132:responder. Steps in between work with entities.
133:### Request body and validation
134:- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
135:  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
136:  first step publishes it as a variable.
137:- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
138:  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
139:  invalid body can return 400.
140:### Transactions
141:`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
142:listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
143:the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.
144:### Errors
145:Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
146:Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
147:`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
148:`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
149:anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.
150:### Security
151:Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:
152:```yaml
153:composition:
154:  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
155:```

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

The `restricted` role works and its main test passes. The three other scenarios in the spec still fail, and I don't think my change caused it: in all three, no page is ever opened as a restricted user. I didn't revert my change to prove they failed before it.

**What I changed**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V112__role_restricted.sql`, allows `restricted` as a stored role.
- **Server:** setting a role now accepts `restricted`; anything else, such as `x`, is still refused with the form's error.
- **Front end:**
  - The roles form offers `restricted`.
  - For a restricted user, the people list shows only the person with their name and the people of every crew that person leads or belongs to. If no person has their name, the list is empty.
  - Everything else (totals row, header, summary, periods, pools) still counts everyone, because only the list rows are filtered.
  - The hook that looks up a user's role moved from the dashboard into `features/roles/roles.slot.tsx` so both places use it. A delegation in force still makes someone a steward, so a delegated restricted user sees everyone.

**Test results** (`PORT=3017 bin/e2e`)
- ✓ `restricted role`, the main test: rows hidden and shown as crews change, an empty list for `vic`, figures over the whole sheet, and the audit lines.
- ✘ Scenario 1, line 560: it expects a claim split off from another to have no tags. The app copies the tags on purpose (`SaveSplit.java:44`).
- ✘ Scenario 2, line 926: it expects the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in when the spec was written, so no app can pass this line.
- ✘ Scenario 3, line 1240: it expects a claim that was just added (and never opened) to be `SETTLED`. My guess is the spec lists claims by date while this app lists them newest-created first, so the test picks up a different row.

I haven't changed split tags or claim ordering to fit the spec, because both are outside this request and would alter behaviour other features rely on. Tell me if you want either one changed.

**Decision for you:** I left actions as they are, so a restricted user is not in the default lists of who may open, settle, void or close claims. The request only covered what they can see. If they should act like a clerk, it's a short change in `Permissions.java`.

**Note on running the tests:** your shell sets `PORT=3002`, and an app from Oct 23 that isn't from this session is already on that port. A plain `bin/e2e` therefore runs the tests against that older app and everything fails. I left those processes alone and ran on port 3017 instead.
